target_customer: iOS app developers and product teams who want to see how real users interact with their apps
problem: Developers could not see where users got stuck inside a live app, and conventional analytics showed numbers without the screen context.
business_model: Usage-based SaaS SDK priced by recordings per month (free under 100, $19 for 100 to 500, $69 for 500 to 3,000 at launch)
product_category: Mobile app session recording and analytics

founders.name: Ishaan Gulrajani
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Zain Shah
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article of 2013-08-08, not on the YC page. Background not found.

exit.reason: Not stated. YC lists the company as Inactive and the company site now returns 404.

competitors.name: UserTesting
competitors.what: Paid panels of testers who use a company's product while recording their screens and voices

competitors.name: Usabilla
competitors.what: User feedback and testing panels for websites and apps

technical_complexity.rationale: Recording an iOS app's screen and touches efficiently, encrypting and storing video, and pixelating private fields needed real SDK engineering from a two person team, though not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: An SDK embedded in apps adds some switching cost, but the launch article shows pricing tiers and a feature set that rivals could copy, and the product was positioned as a complement to analytics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition by an incumbent was found. The company is listed as Inactive without a stated cause.

market_need_then: Mobile app usage was growing quickly in 2013 and the TechCrunch launch coverage described developers wanting to watch real sessions in beta and live apps. Named early customers included SmugMug, Directr and Streak.

branding.domain_note: Used watchsend.com, the exact name as a .com. The domain now returns 404.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain product pitch: videos of your iOS apps

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search returned nothing about the name, logo or community. The only brand evidence is the YC one liner and a TechCrunch launch article, so the brand was forgettable at its peak.

outcome_analysis: Watchsend launched a video based session recording SDK for iOS apps during YC Summer 2013 and had raised a reported seed round of about $650K from angels and small funds shortly before the batch. It had paying tiers and named customers at launch, but no later funding, acquisition or shutdown announcement was found. The cause of the Inactive status is not public, so failure factors are left empty. Later rivals in mobile session replay such as Appsee and UXCam appear in alternatives lists, but those lists are undated and are not counted as competition at founding.
notes: Seed round rests on StartupIntros (fetched) and a Crunchbase snippet that gives the same $650K and May 2013 date, so effectively database sources only. Investors come from StartupIntros only; a separate search snippet named only Scott Banister. The round date is about a month before the Summer 2013 batch, so it predates YC. The company site returned 404 on fetch. Dealroom lists the company as closed but gives no date or reason. Alternatives named on StackShare and Product Hunt (Lookback, Appsee, UXCam) are undated and excluded from competition_at_founding. Founder education and prior employers not found.
